key_insight: DFT predicts that GeC/ReS₂ favors direct Z-scheme charge transfer, enabling overall photocatalytic water splitting with strain-tunable performance.
engineering_relevance: The heterostructure offers a computationally promising route to solar hydrogen production, with predicted solar-to-hydrogen efficiency increasing from 41.40% without strain to 60.68% at +6% tensile strain.
method: First-principles DFT assessment of stability and electronic structure.
Band-alignment and Gibbs free-energy analysis of type-II versus Z-scheme pathways.
Evaluation of pH-dependent water-splitting energetics and strain-dependent efficiency.
evidence_signal: Calculations indicate a 1.38 eV indirect band gap, favorable Z-scheme HER energetics at pH 0–14, and light-driven spontaneous OER at pH 4–14.
watch_item: The efficiencies are computational predictions; experimental validation must establish achievable strain, charge-transfer dynamics, and sustained catalytic performance.
paper_title: Photocatalytic Water Splitting in GeC/ReS$_2$ van der Waals Heterostructures
